summary: Capcom's foundational fighting-game series, covering the arcade mainline, Street Fighter II and Alpha revisions, Street Fighter III/IV/V/6, EX games, major Street Fighter-branded crossovers, puzzle/super-deformed spinoffs, and modern anthology releases.

entries.title: Street Fighter
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: MAME is the preservation fallback for the arcade board if not using the official anthology.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: The 30th Anniversary Collection includes the original arcade Street Fighter in a modern official anthology on current platforms, avoiding the compromised home-computer ports and the renamed Turbo CD version.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection on PC, PS4, Xbox One, or Switch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Home-computer and Turbo CD versions are historically interesting but not preferable for fidelity.

entries.title: Street Fighter 2010: The Final Fight
entries.definitive_edition: Original NES release

emulation.notes: NES emulation is the cleanest preservation route.

primary.why: Street Fighter 2010 is a localized NES action game that is not actually part of the Japanese Street Fighter storyline, but it carries the Street Fighter title in the west and has no enhanced edition.
primary.how_to_play: Play the NES cartridge on hardware or a legally dumped ROM in Mesen.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Japanese version had no Street Fighter connection; treat it as a title/localization curiosity, not core canon.

entries.title: Street Fighter II: The World Warrior
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation only if not using the official collection.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: The 30th Anniversary Collection includes the arcade World Warrior version on modern platforms, making it the best official route for the original SFII revision.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter II in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection; use later SFII entries separately for their added characters and systems.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat later SFII revisions as the same game when cataloging version differences.

entries.title: Street Fighter II: Champion Edition
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: Champion Edition's main additions are playable bosses, mirror matches, balance changes, and alternate colors; the 30th Anniversary Collection supplies the arcade version on modern platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play Champion Edition in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection.

entries.remaster_caveats: Some console releases bundle Champion Edition behavior inside other named SFII products.

entries.title: Street Fighter II: Hyper Fighting
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation if not using the official collection.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: Hyper Fighting adds faster speed, balance changes, and new special moves; the 30th Anniversary Collection includes the arcade version and supports online play for this title.
primary.how_to_play: Play Hyper Fighting in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection.

entries.remaster_caveats: Console ports often have version-specific balance and presentation differences.

entries.title: Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: Arcade emulation is a fallback for preservation.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: Super Street Fighter II adds Cammy, Fei Long, T. Hawk, Dee Jay, revised audiovisuals, and additional colors; the 30th Anniversary Collection provides the arcade version.
primary.how_to_play: Play Super Street Fighter II in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection.

secondary.exclusive_content: The 30th Anniversary Collection Switch version includes a local eight-player Tournament Battle mode for Super Street Fighter II.
secondary.what_to_play: Try the Switch-exclusive Tournament Battle mode if local multi-system play is available.
secondary.why: It is a platform-exclusive mode in the anthology, not core arcade content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Super Turbo and Ultra Street Fighter II are separate later revisions.

entries.title: Super Street Fighter II Turbo
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: Use arcade emulation if the official collection is unavailable.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: Super Turbo adds Super Combos and Akuma and remains a tournament-staple revision; the 30th Anniversary Collection supplies the arcade version with online support.
primary.how_to_play: Play Super Street Fighter II Turbo in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection.

secondary.exclusive_content: Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix has redrawn HD graphics and rebalanced remix options.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample HD Remix if the redrawn presentation is specifically desired.
secondary.why: It is a distinct remix rather than the preferred arcade-authentic Super Turbo route.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD Remix and Ultra Street Fighter II are separate remixes with changed presentation/content.

entries.title: Street Fighter: The Movie
entries.definitive_edition: Original arcade release

emulation.notes: Arcade preservation route.

primary.why: The arcade Street Fighter: The Movie is a distinct digitized-fighter arcade release based on the live-action film; no official modern anthology release supersedes it.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade board or a legally preserved arcade dump in MAME.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not merge with the PlayStation/Saturn game; they are distinct products.

entries.title: Street Fighter: The Movie (console)
entries.definitive_edition: Sega Saturn release

emulation.notes: Saturn emulation is the preservation fallback.

primary.why: The PlayStation/Saturn Street Fighter: The Movie is a separate console fighting game from the arcade release; Saturn is generally the stronger 2D-era console target and preserves the console-specific content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Saturn version on hardware or Mednafen/Saturn emulation; use PlayStation only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official remaster or anthology release is documented in the public list source.

entries.title: Street Fighter Alpha: Warriors' Dreams
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

emulation.notes: Arcade emulation is the fallback.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.version: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version
primary.why: The 30th Anniversary Collection includes the arcade Street Fighter Alpha, preserving the original pre-SFII Alpha entry on modern platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter Alpha in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection; use Alpha Anthology only for its anthology-specific extras.

entries.remaster_caveats: Alpha 2 and Alpha 3 replace/expand the subseries but are distinct games.

entries.title: Street Fighter Alpha 2
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter Alpha Anthology

emulation.notes: PCSX2 for Alpha Anthology; MAME/30th Collection for arcade authenticity.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS2 anthology emulation or arcade anthology

primary.version: Street Fighter Alpha Anthology - Alpha 2 Gold / Zero 2 Alpha route
primary.why: Alpha 2 has several revisions, and Alpha Anthology collects Alpha 2, Alpha 2 Gold/Zero 2 Alpha arrange material, and broader Alpha extras in one package, making it the most complete Alpha 2-focused route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter Alpha Anthology on PS2 or PCSX2; use 30th Anniversary Collection for the arcade-original Alpha 2 version.

secondary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
secondary.exclusive_content: The 30th Anniversary Collection provides the arcade Alpha 2 version on modern platforms.
secondary.what_to_play: Use it for arcade-authentic comparison and modern display/online ecosystem context.
secondary.why: Alpha Anthology is more complete for Alpha 2 variants, while 30th Anniversary is the easier modern arcade route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Pick 30th Anniversary if the goal is strictly arcade Alpha 2 rather than variant coverage.

entries.title: Street Fighter Alpha 3
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter Alpha 3 Max

emulation.notes: PPSSPP for Alpha 3 Max; MAME or official collections for arcade/Upper routes.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PSP emulation for complete content; modern collection for arcade fidelity

primary.why: Alpha 3 Max / Double Upper is the most content-complete named Alpha 3 version, expanding on the arcade and Upper revisions with extra characters and modes, though modern collections are better for arcade presentation.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter Alpha 3 Max on PSP or PPSSPP; use 30th Anniversary Collection for the arcade Alpha 3 version and Capcom Fighting Collection 2 for Alpha 3 Upper.

secondary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
secondary.exclusive_content: 30th Anniversary Collection offers the arcade Alpha 3 version with online-enabled support.
secondary.why: It is not as content-complete as Max but is the best current official arcade route.

secondary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
secondary.exclusive_content: Capcom Fighting Collection 2 includes Street Fighter Alpha 3 Upper.
secondary.what_to_play: Use for the Upper revision on modern platforms.
secondary.why: Upper is a distinct revision between arcade Alpha 3 and PSP Alpha 3 Max.

entries.remaster_caveats: No single modern release combines Max's content with the current anthology presentation.

primary.how_to_play: Play X-Men vs. Street Fighter in Marvel vs. Capcom Fighting Collection: Arcade Classics.

entries.remaster_caveats: This should also be cross-listed mentally with Marvel vs. Capcom, but the title is Street Fighter-branded enough to include here.

entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection arcade version

entries.title: Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike - Fight for the Future

secondary.exclusive_content: 3rd Strike Online Edition has its own presentation and online feature set.

primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter EX2 Plus on PlayStation hardware or DuckStation/Mednafen.

primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with a legally dumped disc.

entries.title: Hyper Street Fighter II: The Anniversary Edition
entries.definitive_edition: Capcom Fighting Collection version

emulation.notes: Use official Capcom Fighting Collection first; arcade/PS2 emulation are preservation alternatives.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.why: Hyper Street Fighter II combines selectable character versions from earlier SFII revisions and has a current official route through Capcom Fighting Collection.
primary.how_to_play: Play Hyper Street Fighter II in Capcom Fighting Collection.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not included in Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection; use Capcom Fighting Collection instead.

entries.title: Street Fighter IV
entries.definitive_edition: Ultra Street Fighter IV

emulation.notes: Use the native PC version for the primary.

primary.why: Ultra Street Fighter IV is the final major SFIV revision and includes the expanded roster/systems over base IV, Super, and Arcade Edition; PC offers the highest-fidelity main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Ultra Street Fighter IV on PC/Steam with current patches; use base Street Fighter IV only for historical comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Base IV, Super, and Arcade Edition remain separate revision history but not the best full play route.

entries.title: Super Street Fighter IV
entries.definitive_edition: Super Street Fighter IV: 3D Edition for unique Super content; Ultra SFIV for full SFIV family

emulation.notes: Use 3DS hardware or emulation for the unique 3D Edition.

primary.why: As its own entry, Super Street Fighter IV's unique 3DS release adds stereoscopic 3D and handheld-specific presentation, while Ultra Street Fighter IV is the better overall SFIV-family route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Super Street Fighter IV: 3D Edition on 3DS for its unique features; play Ultra Street Fighter IV on PC for the definitive SFIV family.

secondary.exclusive_content: Ultra Street Fighter IV contains later roster/system expansion beyond Super.
secondary.what_to_play: Use Ultra for the full SFIV-family playthrough.
secondary.why: Super's 3DS version is unique, but Ultra is more complete.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat Super as the endpoint of the SFIV line.

entries.title: Ultra Street Fighter IV
entries.definitive_edition: Ultra Street Fighter IV on PC

emulation.notes: Use native PC.

primary.why: Ultra Street Fighter IV is the final SFIV revision and the PC version offers the best fidelity/settings route while keeping the full Ultra content package.
primary.how_to_play: Play Ultra Street Fighter IV on Steam/PC with current patches.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later SFIV edition supersedes Ultra.

entries.title: Super Street Fighter II Turbo HD Remix
entries.definitive_edition: Original HD Remix digital release

emulation.notes: Use original consoles if owned; emulation support may vary.

primary.why: HD Remix is a distinct redrawn/rebalanced version of Super Turbo and exists only as a PS3/Xbox 360 digital release.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS3 or Xbox 360 if already owned; otherwise use Super Turbo in 30th Anniversary Collection for the classic route.

entries.remaster_caveats: For classic Super Turbo, use the 30th Anniversary Collection rather than HD Remix.

entries.title: Street Fighter X Tekken
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus PlayStation-exclusive character sampling

emulation.notes: Use native PC; RPCS3/Vita3K only for preservation of PlayStation variants.

primary.why: Street Fighter X Tekken is a crossover fighter released on HD platforms and PC; PC offers the highest-fidelity route, while the PlayStation versions contain platform-exclusive guest characters.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with available updates/DLC for the main run; sample the PlayStation versions for Sony-exclusive characters if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: Sony-platform guest characters are exclusive to the PlayStation versions.
secondary.what_to_play: Play exhibition matches with the PlayStation-exclusive characters.
secondary.why: Those characters are absent from the PC primary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: DLC availability can depend on storefront status and ownership.

entries.title: Street Fighter X Mega Man
entries.definitive_edition: Free Windows release

emulation.notes: Use native Windows compatibility.

primary.why: Street Fighter X Mega Man is a free PC crossover platformer released by Capcom, and PC is its native platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play the free Windows release from Capcom-preserved/downloadable sources where available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability depends on Capcom's current hosting/mirrors.

entries.title: Street Fighter V
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter V: Champion Edition with later DLC content

emulation.notes: Use native PC for the primary.

primary.version: Street Fighter V: Champion Edition with Season V / All Characters content where owned
primary.why: Champion Edition is the expanded SFV package with the major mode/balance updates and first four seasons of content, and the later Season V/All Characters content completes the roster beyond the original CE package; PC is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter V: Champion Edition on PC with the Champion Edition upgrade and Season V/all-character content installed where available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Base and Arcade Edition packages are historical stepping stones, not the final SFV recommendation.

entries.title: Ultra Street Fighter II: The Final Challengers
entries.definitive_edition: Original Nintendo Switch release

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch hardware.

primary.why: Ultra Street Fighter II is a Switch-exclusive revision of SFII with additional characters and modern/classic visual options, distinct from arcade Super Turbo.
primary.how_to_play: Play Ultra Street Fighter II: The Final Challengers on Nintendo Switch.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not use this as a replacement for documenting Super Turbo's arcade version.

entries.title: Street Fighter 30th Anniversary Collection
entries.definitive_edition: PC version plus Switch tournament-mode sampling

emulation.notes: Use native PC or console versions.

primary.platform: PC / PS4 / Xbox One / Nintendo Switch
primary.why: This anthology contains twelve classic arcade Street Fighter titles plus archival materials, with online-enabled versions of Hyper Fighting, Super Turbo, Alpha 3, and 3rd Strike; it is the core modern route for the pre-IV arcade lineage.
primary.how_to_play: Play the collection on PC, PS4, Xbox One, or Switch; choose Switch if the Super Street Fighter II local Tournament Battle mode matters.

secondary.exclusive_content: Switch includes an exclusive local eight-player tournament mode for Super Street Fighter II.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the Switch version for that local mode.
secondary.why: It is an exclusive anthology feature.

entries.remaster_caveats: The collection omits Hyper Street Fighter II and several Alpha anthology extras, which need separate entries/collections.

entries.title: Street Fighter: Duel
entries.definitive_edition: Current mobile release

emulation.notes: Use a compatible mobile device.

primary.why: Street Fighter: Duel is a mobile RPG/idle-battle spinoff that launched first in China and then worldwide; mobile is its only official route.
primary.how_to_play: Install Street Fighter: Duel on a compatible iOS or Android device in a supported region.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service content and regional availability can change over time.

entries.title: Street Fighter 6
entries.definitive_edition: Street Fighter 6 Years 1-2 Fighters Edition / current DLC build on PC

emulation.notes: Use native PC for the primary.

primary.version: Street Fighter 6 Years 1-2 Fighters Edition / current DLC build
primary.why: Street Fighter 6 launched on PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, later adding a Switch 2 Years 1-2 Fighters Edition; PC remains the highest-fidelity main route, while the Years 1-2 package is the most complete edition baseline for the first two DLC years.
primary.how_to_play: Play Street Fighter 6 on PC with the Years 1-2 Fighters Edition content or equivalent DLC installed; use current patches.

secondary.exclusive_content: Switch 2 version adds platform-specific modes such as motion/party features while including Years 1-2 content.
secondary.why: PC is the fidelity primary, but Switch 2 has platform-specific extras.

entries.remaster_caveats: DLC seasons continue beyond the initial launch package; keep the entry current as new fighter-year bundles release.

entries.title: Street Fighter VR Shadaloo Enhancement Plan
entries.definitive_edition: Original arcade VR release

emulation.notes: No public home/emulation route exists.

primary.why: Street Fighter VR Shadaloo Enhancement Plan is a Japanese arcade VR attraction/game, not a home fighting-game release, and has no documented home port.
primary.how_to_play: Play at supported Japanese arcade/VR locations if available; otherwise treat as a location-based preservation edge case.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability is location-dependent and may change as arcade installations rotate.
